title: Language of Sequences & Series

blocks.md: - A **progression** (or **sequence**) is an ***ordered*** set of numbers with a rule for finding all the numbers in the progression** **

blocks.alt: Lang Seq Ser Illustr 1, A Level & AS Level Pure Maths Revision Notes

blocks.md:
- The numbers in a sequence are called **terms**
- The terms of a progression are often referred to by letters with a subscript

blocks.alt: Lang Seq Ser Illustr 2, A Level & AS Level Pure Maths Revision Notes

blocks.md: - You get a **series** by summing up the terms in a **progression***** ***

blocks.alt: Lang Seq Ser Illustr 3, A Level & AS Level Pure Maths Revision Notes

blocks.md: - We use the notation ***S***<sub>***n ***</sub>to refer to the sum of the first ***n*** terms in the progression ie.   ***S***<sub>***n***</sub>** =** ***u***<sub>**1**</sub>** +***** u***<sub>**2**</sub>*** *****+ *****u***<sub>**3**</sub>** + … + *****u***<sub>**n**</sub>

blocks.alt: Lang Seq Ser Illustr 4, A Level & AS Level Pure Maths Revision Notes

blocks.text: What are increasing, decreasing and periodic progressions?

blocks.md:
- A progression is **increasing** if ***u***<sub>***n***</sub><sub>**+1**</sub>** > *****u***<sub>***n***</sub> for all positive integers ***n*** – ie if every term is greater than the term before it
- A progression is **decreasing** if ***u***<sub>***n***</sub><sub>**+1**</sub>** < *****u***<sub>***n***</sub> for all positive integers ***n*** – ie if every term is less than the term before it

blocks.alt: Lang Seq Ser Illustr 5, A Level & AS Level Pure Maths Revision Notes

blocks.md:
- A progression is **periodic** if the terms repeat in a cycle
- The **order** (or **period**) of a periodic progression is the number of terms in each repeating cycle

blocks.alt: Lang Seq Ser Illustr 6, A Level & AS Level Pure Maths Revision Notes

blocks.label: Exam Hint
blocks.md:
Look out for progressions defined by trigonometric functions – this can be a way of 'hiding' a periodic function.
